outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to the Efficiency Crisis in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by analyzing the current limitations of modern Large Language Models (LLMs), focusing on the trade-offs between model performance and resource efficiency. It introduces the concept of quantization as a primary solution and contrasts traditional post-training quantization with architectural changes required for true 1-bit computing.
subtopics: The exponential growth of LLM sizes and associated environmental/economic costs
The dominance of matrix multiplication in transformer inference
Limitations of Post-Training Quantization (PTQ): Why moving from FP16 to 4-bit is sub-optimal
The theoretical shift from Floating Point Arithmetic to Integer Addition

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Theoretical Foundations of BitNet b1.58 Architecture
outline.description: A deep dive into the core innovations of the BitNet b1.58 architecture. Students will learn how replacing standard linear layers with ternary-weighted layers transforms the computational paradigm, enabling exact matching of full-precision models while drastically reducing complexity.
subtopics: From Binary (-1, +1) to Ternary {-1, 0, 1}: Understanding 'Bits' vs. 'Effective Bits'
Why 0 matters: Explicit feature filtering and enhanced modeling capability
The replacement of nn.Linear with BitLinear layers
Computation Paradigm Shift: Eliminating Multiplication via Integer Addition

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Mathematical Mechanics and Training Dynamics
outline.description: This chapter details the mathematical formulations governing weight constraint and activation handling in BitNet b1.58. It covers the specific quantization functions used during training and how they differ from previous iterations like vanilla BitNet.
subtopics: The absmean Quantization Function: Scaling by Average Absolute Value ($\gamma$)
Mathematical derivation of RoundClip constraints for weights {-1, 0, 1}
Activation Handling: Per-token scaling to [-Qb, Qb] vs. Zero-point removal
